entry.title: Part 3: Partitioning & Clustering for Performance 🚀
entry.summary:
This is where BigQuery optimization gets really powerful! These two techniques can reduce your query costs by 90% or more. Imagine you have a table with 5 years of taxi trip data - about 500 million rows. Every time you query: SELECT * FROM taxi_trips WHERE pickup_date = '2024-01-15';
Without optimization, BigQuery scans ALL 500 million rows just to find trips from one day. That's: Slow (lots of data to read) Expensive (you pay for all data scanned) Wasteful (you only needed 0.05% of the data!) Partitioning and clustering solve this problem! Think of partitioning like organizing a filing cabinet. Instead of one giant drawer with all documents, you have: Drawer for January Drawer for February Drawer for March ...and so on When you need something from March, you ONLY open the March drawer! …

BigQuery is Google's data warehouse in the cloud. It's one of the most popular choices for storing and analyzing large amounts of data because it's: Serverless - You don't manage any servers. No installing software, no worrying about disk space, no maintenance. Google handles everything.
